overview: A nationwide air traffic system ground stop caused by a telecoms network upgrade highlighted chronic infrastructure vulnerabilities. In San Francisco, ongoing fallout from the Nvidia scandal tests political alliances and shines a light on AI industry intelligence risks, while Marina Safeway litigation moves forward. In Hawaii, Kali Watson is stepping down as the director of the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands.

wiki.title: Aucanquilcha
wiki.extract: Aucanquilcha is a large compound volcano in the Antofagasta Region of northern Chile, within the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes. The volcano has the form of a ridge reaching an altitude of 6,176 metres (20,262 ft) above sea level, formed between 1.04 and 0.23 million years ago; there is ongoing fumarolic activity. The volcano is part of a larger cluster of volcanoes sometimes known as the "Aucanquilcha cluster" or "Aucanquilcha complex". This cluster includes lava domes and lava flows that have formed in several stages over 11 million years of activity with varying magma output. During the ice ages, Aucanquilcha was covered in an ice cap that left moraines and cirques.
